headline: Sheikh Hasina plan to return and surrender around December
summary: The ousted prime minister told Reuters that she and senior Awami League leaders intend to voluntarily return to Bangladesh from exile in India.
details: Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told Reuters in a telephone interview that she and senior Awami League colleagues plan to return to Bangladesh around December and surrender to the authorities.
Hasina, 78, stated that she intends to return voluntarily to present herself in court, despite facing a death sentence in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on student-led protests.
She expressed that her party leaders and workers are facing 'tremendous repression' and stated, 'If death comes, I want it to come on my own soil.'
Hasina fled the country in 2024 after protests ended her 20-year tenure as prime minister. A UN report indicates that the crackdown leading to her downfall killed as many as 1,400 people.
The former prime minister mentioned that the authorities in Dhaka are repeatedly sending letters to India seeking her extradition, but she insists she will return on her own terms.
She has not consulted with any foreign government regarding the timing or specific court for her surrender, and she noted that she is not worried about jail time.
A return could potentially improve strained ties between Bangladesh and India, which deteriorated after New Delhi gave her refuge.
Hasina also mentioned that she has been holding online meetings to reorganize the Awami League, emphasizing that the people should decide the party's political rights.
caption:
Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh in December to surrender in court, despite facing a death sentence.

Ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told Reuters in a telephone interview that she and senior Awami League colleagues plan to return to Bangladesh around December and surrender to the authorities.

Hasina, 78, stated that she intends to return voluntarily to present herself in court, despite facing a death sentence in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on student-led protests.

She expressed that her party leaders and workers are facing 'tremendous repression' and stated, 'If death comes, I want it to come on my own soil.'

Hasina fled the country in 2024 after protests ended her 20-year tenure as prime minister. A UN report indicates that the crackdown leading to her downfall killed as many as 1,400 people.

The former prime minister mentioned that the authorities in Dhaka are repeatedly sending letters to India seeking her extradition, but she insists she will return on her own terms.

She has not consulted with any foreign government regarding the timing or specific court for her surrender, and she noted that she is not worried about jail time.

A return could potentially improve strained ties between Bangladesh and India, which deteriorated after New Delhi gave her refuge.

Hasina also mentioned that she has been holding online meetings to reorganize the Awami League, emphasizing that the people should decide the party's political rights.
